content:
Bishop Hill fully demolished, residents too late to protest

Mr. So said that after receiving the demolition notice at the end of July, he immediately contacted Sham Shui Po District Councillors, hoping to keep the fitness facilities on Woh Tsai Shan (Bishop Hill), but was told in reply that "none of them will be preserved." He said that in previous demolitions he was always able to organise residents to petition and protest, but this time the notice period was too short to mobilise residents to stop the works. As a result, the morning exercise spot that residents had used for over 20 years has come to an end.

Three days ago (10th), the Home Affairs Department announced the "Woh Tsai Shan Optimisation Plan", stating that the government would clear illegal and unsafe structures, facilities or杂物 on the hill in phases, pointing out that these objects had been illegally occupying government land for many years.

Yesterday morning (12th) at around 6:30, Lands Department staff and uniformed police officers arrived, sealing off the Tong Chong Street hillside rest garden from the foot to the top of the hill. Workers then arrived and carried away items including exercise bikes and table tennis tables. Police deployed冲锋车 (PTU vehicles) and 豬籠車 (prisoner transport vehicles) for警戒. Mr. So said the place is merely where residents exercise, and he does not understand the point of the police presence: "The officers just stood there, monitoring the whole time. What are we doing? Are we rioters? Have we broken the law?"

"Morning Exercise Paradise" becomes LCSD facility

Mr. So pointed out that residents collectively raised HK$400,000 to build the "Morning Exercise Paradise" on Bishop Hill, including a table tennis table, fitness equipment, and an unofficial hiking trail built decades ago. On the day of demolition, many residents were still doing morning exercises and using the fitness facilities. Several residents expressed deep regret at the disappearance of the morning exercise spot they had used for years. Some residents kept asking Mr. So what to do, but he too was at a loss.

He said he had spent several consecutive days moving the fitness equipment away, hoping to preserve as much of their hard work as possible. He has already removed all the muscle massage rollers, while some residents plan to move certain deity statues to Lantau Island.

According to the Home Affairs Department's "Woh Tsai Shan Optimisation Plan", the "Morning Exercise Paradise" will be converted into an LCSD facility; the makeshift fitness equipment on the hill will be replaced with standard LCSD recreational and sports facilities; as for the deity statues, religious leaders will visit the site to handle them properly.

Escape from death – building Bishop Hill's "Morning Exercise Paradise"

75-year-old So Chi-keung is a SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) survivor. Due to side effects of medication, he suffered from aftereffects including muscle pain, weakness and fatigue. After three years of physiotherapy, his condition showed no improvement. In 2008, Mr. So was invited by a neighbour to Bishop Hill, and after morning exercise found his spirits improved, which he attributed to the fresh air on the hill. Thereafter he began exercising on Bishop Hill at six every morning. After persisting for a month, he recovered his health and strength and decided to stop physiotherapy.

In 2009, Mr. So travelled to South Korea and was inspired by the fitness facilities there. After returning to Hong Kong, he took the designs as reference and built exercise bikes and resistance rope machines himself at the hardware factory he ran, then single-handedly carried the disassembled equipment up Bishop Hill. He described the manufacturing process as simple, but hauling the equipment uphill as extremely arduous. The result was that he spent four years building over 20 recreational and sports facilities on Bishop Hill, including swings, balance beams and rollers, and placed them on the vacant land above the current Sham Shui Po Service Reservoir. At the time some elderly residents objected, but after using the equipment residents found it helped relieve physical discomfort, and the facilities became very popular.

Bishop Hill's first exposure – residents protest demolition

Mr. So said that in 2014 over 200 young people held a psychedelic party on Bishop Hill, causing noise nuisance. When police arrived, they discovered for the first time a large number of private fitness facilities. Afterwards, the Water Supplies Department stepped up patrols of Bishop Hill, repeatedly driving away residents exercising on the hill, and planned to demolish the facilities. At that time Mr. So launched multiple protests and went in person to the Sham Shui Po District Council Secretariat to fight for the preservation of the fitness garden.

Accidental check-in – Bishop Hill Service Reservoir becomes a Grade I historic building

In 2017, the Water Supplies Department planned to clear unauthorised structures on Bishop Hill and return the land to the Lands Department. In addition, two large trees on top of the reservoir had roots extending into the structure, posing a collapse risk. In 2020, the authorities prepared to remove the trees and fill in the reservoir. The Water Supplies Department promised Mr. So that his fitness facilities could be placed on the land after backfilling, and Mr. So therefore agreed to the works.

The result was that on Christmas Eve, Mr. So and a volunteer seized the chance to sneak into the reservoir to check whether anything had been left behind, taking photos and uploading them to social media. This attracted large numbers of citizens to check in at the reservoir, drawing public attention. Mr. So said that the public at that time protested the demolition because of the reservoir's historical value. Ms. Fong, a resident who often visits Bishop Hill, even stood in front of an excavator at one point to halt the demolition works.

In 2021, the reservoir was graded as a Grade I historic building by the Antiquities Advisory Board, and the reservoir was preserved and opened to the public. Mr. So relocated the fitness facilities to the foot of the hill.

The Mao Zedong statue incident may have been the trigger for the demolition

In June 2022, the Sham Shui Po District Management Committee wanted to remove the altar and fitness facilities. Mr. So launched a signature campaign to fight for their preservation, stating that a total of 3,399 Sham Shui Po district residents signed, and submitted a letter to the Home Affairs Department, pledging that no further expansion of facilities would be carried out.

Mr. So said that thereafter Bishop Hill remained peaceful, with no indication from the government of demolition. But in early 2026, resident Ms. Fong erected a Mao Zedong statue and Mao Zedong Cultural Hall on Bishop Hill, which were subsequently removed. Mr. So believes the Mao Zedong incident brought the government to refocus on Bishop Hill. Combined with some residents making loud noise on the hill and disturbing nearby residents, the government therefore decided to clear Bishop Hill completely.

In early 2026, resident Ms. Fong erected a Mao Zedong statue and a Mao Zedong Cultural Hall on Bishop Hill, reigniting the controversy over the hill's use. (File photo)

"Without Bishop Hill, I'd have lived 20 years less"

Watching workers dismantle piece by piece the fitness facilities he had built with his own hands, Mr. So did not show sadness. He plans to move the dismantled equipment back to his home, and has been telling the media about the history of Bishop Hill. In fact, he knows full well that the "Morning Exercise Paradise" has been in breach of regulations and controversial for years, but he believes the place has benefited many residents. He hopes that by telling the story of Bishop Hill, he can gain recognition from the government. Although he ultimately failed to preserve it, he still hopes to pass the story on, in gratitude for what Bishop Hill has given him.

He bid farewell to Bishop Hill: "I am grateful it gave me a new life. Without it, I would not have had those 20 years, I should have died. If it were not for Bishop Hill, I would have died long ago… Besides, I am an injured SARS survivor, do you think I could have lived to today?"
